summary:
Nexium is an interactive web story about 27 abandoned machines on the Moon, Mars, Venus and Titan. Visitors rotate 3D globes, read each machine’s story, and explore timelines, instruments, NASA image search and quizzes. A kids’ mode presents each machine as a conversation between an alien and an astronaut, followed by a quiz. An AI guide, Nex, answers questions from the site’s content.

It fits the challenge by treating discarded equipment as characters with stories, backed by verified facts and sources. It matters because it makes space exploration history accessible to learners of all ages.
details:
Nexium is an interactive web story about 27 machines abandoned on the Moon, Mars, Venus and Titan, from Surveyor 1 (1966) to Pragyan (2023). Each machine is told as a character with a narrative, next to sourced facts.

What it does: visitors rotate 3D globes of the Moon, Mars, Venus and Titan and click a machine to read its story. They can search and filter the machine cards, follow a timeline from 1967 to 2026, learn about the scientific instruments, search the NASA image archive, and play quizzes, word and ordering games, and a story-matching game. An accessibility panel offers text size, contrast, letter spacing, monochrome, a dyslexia-friendly font and reduced motion.

How it works and tools: a single-page site built with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, with images and maps from NASA, JPL and public-domain archives, hosted on GitHub Pages. The Nex guide sends questions to a small Cloudflare Worker, which keeps the Groq API key on the server; if the service is unavailable, Nex falls back to built-in answers. AI development assistance: Claude.

Kids mode and learning design: children first meet each machine in a short conversation between a green alien and an astronaut, where the facts come up naturally as questions and answers. Then a five-question quiz asks them to work out the answer from what they just read, so they test themselves rather than only reading. Stars and badges reward their progress. The Nex guide is a helper for exploring the site, not a replacement for discovery.

Intended impact: discarded equipment becomes a way to teach planetary science, engineering and the history of exploration to learners of all ages, including students who find long texts hard to read. Creativity: each machine is a storyteller, the kids mode uses a conversation format, and the site explores abandoned hardware the way a museum would.
